decisive_items: Ascites culture yielded growth of Escherichia coli
edema in all layers of intestinal wall, predominant thickening and edema in submucosa, diffuse infiltration of neutrophils with presence of abscesses
Bacterial colonies observed in submucosa surrounding the ESD lesion
response.rationale: The E. coli-positive ascites and histologic findings of neutrophil-rich abscesses with bacterial colonies around the ESD site indicate an acute bacterial infectious colitis localized to the ascending colon, with no CT evidence of perforation. R7C is preferred over R7 because the bacterial qualifier is directly supported; typhlitis is less likely because there is no profound neutropenia or cecal-predominant pattern.

rejected.why: Typhlitis requires a neutropenic/cecal-predominant pattern; here leukopenia is mild and the lesion is an infected ESD site in the ascending colon.
Fever and inflammatory markers are only mildly elevated with no organ dysfunction/hypotension; findings are primarily localized colonic infection.
No ischemic risk factors or vascular pattern; histology shows acute suppurative infection rather than ischemic necrosis.
Acute E. coli infection/abscesses and no prior bowel symptoms do not support chronic inflammatory bowel disease.
No diverticula are described; clinical and histologic evidence points to colitis at the ascending colon ESD site.
CT explicitly states no perforation, and neither imaging nor pathology demonstrates a perforation tract.
Peritoneal signs are right-sided, but CT/histology implicate the ascending colon rather than the appendix, with no appendiceal inflammation described.
Thrombocytopenia alone is insufficient; there are no schistocytes, neurologic changes, or renal/microangiopathic features.
